prose: John Gruber flags Rolfe Winkler's WSJ story on Apple's chip suppliers getting their revenge, quoting its color: Tony Blevins, Apple's feared procurement chief until 2022, scheduled back-to-back meetings so rival supplier sales teams would run into each other, and reps packed nutrition bars for negotiating sessions Apple pushed past midnight without a dinner break. The piece chronicles how that leverage has now flipped to the suppliers.
highlights: WSJ on Apple's supplier leverage flipping to the chip sellers
Blevins lore: staged rival run-ins, past-midnight sessions without dinner
Same story covered from the supply side in 'Money and chips' (WSJ original)
